habitat.naturalHabitat: Human colon — one of the most abundant members of normal gut flora
habitat.hostAssociation: Normal commensal of the large intestine; opportunistic pathogen when it escapes the gut
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Not a significant free-living environmental organism

microscopy.appearance: Gram-negative pleomorphic rods, often faintly/unevenly staining

culture.media: Bacteroides bile esculin (BBE) agar, anaerobic blood agar
culture.growthCharacteristics: Obligate anaerobe; grows in the presence of 20% bile (unusual among anaerobes), aiding selective isolation

identificationClues: Gram-negative anaerobic rod that, unusually for an anaerobe, tolerates and even grows better with bile
Growth on Bacteroides bile esculin (BBE) agar is a key selective/differential feature
Most common anaerobic isolate from intra-abdominal infections and abscesses
Polymicrobial infections are typical — usually recovered alongside facultative anaerobes like E. coli

virulenceFactors: Lipopolysaccharide (less potent endotoxin activity than typical Gram-negative LPS)
Various enzymes (e.g. superoxide dismutase) enhancing survival
clinicalImportance.transmission: Endogenous — arises from the patient's own gut flora following bowel injury, surgery, or perforation, not typically transmitted person-to-person
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: The most frequently isolated anaerobic pathogen in clinical intra-abdominal and pelvic infections
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Bile tolerance is an unusual and useful selective feature, since most other obligate anaerobes are inhibited by bile salts

examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Tolerates and grows well in bile, unusual for an obligate anaerobe
